prompt: Explain why the Nazi Party grew in support between 1929 and 1933.
indicativeContent: The Wall Street Crash/Depression caused mass unemployment, creating demand for radical solutions
Effective Nazi propaganda and the visible strength of the SA gave an impression of order and strength
Nazi promises cut across class lines, appealing to both middle-class and working-class voters
Growing fear of Communism pushed some voters and elites toward the Nazis as an alternative
Political instability and weak coalition governments under the Weimar Constitution made a strong, decisive alternative more appealing
A strong answer explains multiple causes and how they connect, not just lists them

prompt: Two historians study the same event in Nazi Germany but reach different conclusions about how much ordinary Germans supported the regime. Explain why two historians' interpretations of the same event might differ, even when looking at similar evidence.
indicativeContent: Historians may have used different sources (e.g. official Nazi records vs. private diaries/letters) which emphasise different things
A historian's own perspective, time period, or purpose in writing can shape which evidence they prioritise
Some evidence from the period (propaganda, forced public displays of support) is itself unreliable, so historians may weigh it differently
Access to new evidence over time can change later historians' conclusions compared to earlier ones
This is a skills-practice question — in the real exam, you'd be given two actual interpretations to compare directly

levelDescriptors.description: Simple, general comment with little explanation.
